before.title: 48V Ground Connection Overheating and Fire Risk (Recall 24V207)
before.description: On 48V mild-hybrid GLS 450/580 models, the ground cable bolt for the 48V system located under the front passenger seat may not have been tightened to specification at the factory. A loose ground lug increases electrical resistance which, combined with the very high currents the 48V starter-alternator (ISG) draws, can cause the connection to overheat, melt surrounding components and, in the worst case, start a fire. This prompted a U.S. safety recall (NHTSA 24V207) covering roughly 116,020 GLE and GLS vehicles built between June 2017 and January 2023. This is a physical hardware/connection defect distinct from a discharged 48V battery — the connection itself overheats.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform recall 24V207: inspect and re-torque (and if necessary replace) the 48V ground connection under the front passenger seat, free of charge. Owners who notice a burning/electrical smell from the front-passenger floor area, repeated 48V system faults, or warning messages should stop driving and contact Mercedes. Check VIN against the recall at the NHTSA or Mercedes recall lookup.
symptoms: Burning or electrical smell from front passenger floor area
Melted or discolored connection under passenger seat

before.title: 4MATIC Transfer Case Bearing Wear, Whine and Drivetrain Lock-Up Risk
before.description: The 4MATIC transfer case on the GLS is prone to internal bearing wear, typically beginning with fluid degradation or a slow leak from the output/case seals. As the bearings wear, owners report a whining or grinding noise that increases with vehicle speed and worsens over time. On the X167 generation the transfer case is more closely integrated with the 9G-Tronic transmission, so a severe bearing failure can shed metal debris into the transmission, turning a contained repair into a much larger and more expensive one. In the worst case a complete failure can lock the drivetrain or cause sudden loss of drive. Running mismatched/uneven tires accelerates the wear.
before.solution: Service the transfer case fluid on a preventive interval (Mercedes does not list a fixed interval, but enthusiasts recommend roughly every 60,000 miles) and address any seal leak promptly to keep the fluid full. Investigate any speed-dependent whine early with a fluid inspection for metal particles. Always replace all four tires together with matching brand/size/wear to avoid driveline bind. A failed transfer case typically runs into the thousands, and far more if debris damages the transmission.
symptoms: Whining noise that rises with speed
Sudden loss of power / drivetrain lock-up in severe cases

before.title: Engine Stall from Transmission Control Unit Software (Recall 24V118)
before.description: Certain X167 GLS 450 (and V167 GLE 450) vehicles left the factory with transmission control unit (TCU) software that does not meet current specifications. If a downshift of the 9G-Tronic from 7th to 6th gear is not fully completed during a light braking maneuver, and several conditions coincide (an aborted shift, low transmission oil temperature, and simultaneous energy recuperation by the 48V starter-alternator), the engine can stall unexpectedly. A stall while driving increases crash risk. This is a software/calibration stall fault, distinct from the existing harsh-shift complaint. NHTSA recall 24V118 (announced Feb 2024) covers approximately 105,071 MY2020-2023 GLE 450 and GLS 450 vehicles. After a stall the engine can be restarted, and steering/braking remain functional.
before.solution: Have the dealer install the updated transmission control unit software under recall 24V118 — a free reflash that typically takes under 30 minutes. Owners experiencing unexpected stalls during gentle braking/deceleration should reference this recall and verify their VIN through the Mercedes or NHTSA recall lookup.
symptoms: Engine restarts after coming to a stop

before.title: M256 Engine Excessive Oil Consumption and Piston Ring Wear
before.description: Owners of GLS 450 models with the M256 3.0L turbocharged inline-six report elevated oil consumption that tends to surface at higher mileage (commonly reported around 60,000 miles / ~100,000 km). The pattern — oil disappearing without visible external leaks — points to internal piston ring / cylinder wear as the likely cause, and in some documented cases correcting it required significant engine disassembly. There is no factory recall specifically for piston rings/oil consumption on the M256 as of 2026, so repairs typically fall on the owner once out of warranty.
before.solution: Monitor oil level frequently between services and keep records of consumption rate to support a goodwill/warranty claim. Use only Mercedes-spec (MB 229.x) low-ash synthetic oil and avoid extended drain intervals. If consumption exceeds roughly 1 quart per 1,000 miles, have the dealer perform a documented oil-consumption test; persistent excessive consumption may require piston ring or short-block work.
symptoms: Oil level dropping without visible leaks
Frequent need to top up oil

before.title: OM656 Diesel CP4 High-Pressure Fuel Pump Sensitivity and Injector Damage
before.description: The OM656 diesel uses a precise Bosch CP4 common-rail high-pressure fuel pump that reacts poorly to low-quality diesel or fuel contamination. Even minor tank impurities or a single mis-fueling event can damage the pump and injection nozzles, and metallic debris from a failing CP4 can circulate through the fuel system. Clogged fuel filters from contaminated fuel further disrupt combustion and cause power loss. Repairs can be extensive because a failed CP4 may require cleaning or replacing injectors, lines and the high-pressure pump. This is an EU-relevant concern given diesel availability and variable fuel quality across markets.
before.solution: Fuel only with high-quality diesel from reputable stations and never mis-fuel with petrol. Replace the fuel filter(s) on schedule. At the first sign of a hard start, rough running, or fuel-system warning, stop driving and have the fuel system inspected — catching CP4 wear early can avoid a full fuel-system contamination repair. If metallic debris is found, the pump, lines and injectors typically all require service.

before.title: OM656 Diesel Emissions System Clogging (EGR/DPF/AdBlue SCR) and Limp Mode
before.description: EU-market GLS 350d/400d models with the OM656 3.0L inline-six diesel suffer from sensitivity in the exhaust aftertreatment chain. The EGR (AGR) valve, diesel particulate filter (DPF) and SCR/AdBlue system are sensitive to poor fuel quality, short-trip driving and temperature swings. Clogged DPF, a dirty/sticking EGR valve, or a faulty EGR differential-pressure sensor cause power loss, failed regenerations, dashboard warnings and limp-home mode. A German motor-talk owner thread on the GLS X167 400d documents poor acceleration that resolves after a restart, traced to a replaced EGR differential-pressure sensor under warranty. This primarily affects diesels not sold in the US, so it is especially relevant to the EU market.
before.solution: Drive the vehicle regularly at highway speed/load to allow active DPF regeneration to complete; avoid chronic short trips. Keep AdBlue topped up with spec-compliant fluid. Have a clogged DPF forced-regenerated or cleaned, and replace a sticking EGR valve or faulty EGR differential-pressure sensor as needed. Use good-quality diesel to reduce soot loading. Address fault codes promptly before forced regen damages the DPF.
symptoms: Repeated regeneration cycles or failed regen

before.title: Panoramic Sunroof Water Leak
before.description: The large panoramic sunroof on the X167 GLS develops water leaks at the drain tubes or seal interface. Water enters the headliner and can drip into the cabin, staining the headliner and potentially damaging the overhead electronics.
before.solution: Clear the sunroof drain tubes with compressed air. Reseal the sunroof glass to the frame if the weatherstrip has shifted. If the headliner is water-stained, it may need cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Water dripping from overhead console area
Damp headliner after rain or car wash

citations.title: MBWorld.org - X167 GLS panoramic sunroof leak reports and fixes

communityRecommendations.content: Avoid automated car washes with high-pressure nozzles pointed at the roof. The extreme water pressure overwhelms the sunroof seals and drains. Hand wash or touchless wash only.

proposal.title: Panoramic Sunroof Water Leak
proposal.description: The reviewed GLS corpus contains no exact Mercedes communication or recall establishing panoramic-roof drain-tube or seal leakage across model years 2020-2025. The only targeted sunroof records concern gesture-control operation, not water entry. No exact source supports the frozen drain-tube blockage, shifted weatherstrip, headliner damage or compressed-air remedy.
proposal.solution: Document the water entry point and conditions, then perform a controlled low-pressure water test while checking the roof cassette, drains, hose joints, glass alignment, seals and nearby body seams separately. Avoid forcing high-pressure air through a drain until hose routing and attachment are confirmed. Do not buy seals, drain hoses, glass or a headliner from this page; the leak path and fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: water entry point and conditions documented
cassette, seal, hose and body-seam paths separated
